# Resource status — textbook edition 0.48

Assembled 14 October 2026. The private book has 50 draft chapters: Unit 1 has 16, Unit 2 has 10, Unit 3 has 14 and Unit 4 has 10. All four units include review/exam-preparation resources; Unit 4 includes full-course consolidation. Python/SQLite examples use synthetic data.

All four editorial coverage maps are available. Their own edition labels/dates are historical snapshots retained as provenance. No unit is signed off for certified alignment. Independent teacher review, conventions, learner evidence, source currency and pacing remain pending; reference PASS results do not establish achievement.

The plan provides 64 lessons in 16 teaching weeks per semester, with Weeks 17–18 blocked for exams. Projects, assessment slots, feedback and revision fit within that allocation. Unit 3 uses 12 embedded project lessons; Unit 4 uses four foundations and 16 embedded workshops. Confirm actual period length, event losses and the school assessment outline. Starters are unfinished; model solutions apply only to the brief's classroom scope. Practice sets are original formative samples, not endorsed full examinations or secure summative materials. Teacher files are separate but not access-protected.

Resource authoring dates are distinct from the website edition. Recheck legal/source currency before reuse. Ownership, open licence, contribution rights and third-party permissions remain unconfirmed for public release. This private resource has no SCSA or Department endorsement.


## Current public access and reuse — 14 October 2026

The textbook is now public with no account required. Original educational content is CC BY 4.0; original software and runnable Python/SQL example code are MIT-licensed. See [licence scope](LICENSE.md). Source: https://github.com/EdugenIO/cs-atar-textbook . Earlier descriptions above record the private development phase and do not override the current licence notice. The website is a textbook with worksheets, practice questions, quizzes and explained answers; it does not grade, collect submissions or track students.
